description:
Missionary's own send, composed on the Gmail Android app and BCC'd to the ingest address. The paragraph-shape specimen: this client separates paragraphs with an empty block holding a single
, and nothing else in the corpus does.
notes:
The letter body is a flat run of
blocks with no margins on them, and every blank line between paragraphs is a separate

. Deleting those as empty publishes the whole letter as one paragraph, which is exactly what happened to a real message before this capture existed.

The corpus could not have caught that, because every other capture is a forward and a forward is re-composed by the forwarder's desktop client, which spaces paragraphs with margins instead. Only a real send characterises the sending client.
The first line is a bare text node inside the outer div rather than a block of its own, so a body has started before the first break block closes.
Adjacent line blocks with no break between them appear three times -- label and value, the verse block, and the sign-off -- so a rule that inserts spacing per block would be wrong here.

The body ends with a trailing

inside the outer div. Trimming has to reach through the closing tag to remove it.
multipart/alternative with no multipart/related and no attachments: the simplest possible tree, from the client with the most awkward markup.
To: is undisclosed-recipients:; and Bcc: post@pdayletters.com survives in this copy, same as the Gmail web BCC capture.
The Google Photos album link in the body is what linked-photo-service detection reads. Both of the first real letters carried one.
